winner.title: Riz Gras (Fat Rice) from Burkina Faso

evidence.authenticity: Explains national-dish status, French name, link to Senegalese tiebou djen, party dish, why the oil is generous. Traditional tomato/onion/rice one-pot with habanero and bouillon. Author is a US food writer, not from the cuisine; adds curry powder, cinnamon, bay.
evidence.precision: Cups/lb for most items; 'large saucepan' with no size; doneness cues on only a few steps (fragrant, tomato water reduced, rice cooked); 3 carrots and 3 tomatoes unsized. No temperatures.
evidence.testing: Author cooked it and gives tips: garlic burns so lower heat, use a heavy hand with oil, habanero was milder than expected. No test-kitchen process.
evidence.photos: Some photos in the article (finished dish, a mixing shot) but not clearly one per stage. Not confirmed as full process coverage.
evidence.efficiency: Single pot, about 30 minutes active and cook time; no wasted steps. No total time stated.
evidence.access: Habanero and Maggi are easy to find in the US. Article gives Maggi as the bouillon alternative and notes that meat and heat can be changed.

winner.why: Only candidate with real dish context, tested tips and sensible one-pot method, but it still falls under 60 on precision and photos.

runnerUp.title: One-pot Spicy Tomato Rice (Riz Gras)- Burkina Faso

evidence.authenticity: Author admits adding spices not typical of Burkinabe riz gras (garam masala, mustard, fennel) and cutting the oil, which removes the 'fat' idea.
evidence.precision: Cup and tbsp measures, no weights; 1 sensory cue; no pan size or temperatures.
evidence.testing: Little reasoning shown; 4.2 rating from 6 ratings.
evidence.photos: 18 images on page, none in the recipe schema steps; not confirmed as process shots.
evidence.access: Mostly pantry items; chillies and spices are easy to find.

runnerUp.why: Easy to cook but strays from the traditional preparation, so it ranks below the winner.

candidates.source: The Storied Recipe (Ivorian riz au gras via Liz Zunon)

candidates.disqualified: Copy of the Travel by Stove recipe; no process photos
Not the dish: Chinese-style fried rice with soy and sesame oil; ingredient list inconsistent with steps
